subject: Warm-Standby activation lead time & priority window — amendment request
messages:
From: Alice Hart <alice.hart@finledger.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+contracts@finledger.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Warm-Standby activation lead time — proposed amendment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security and ops teams reviewed the Warm-Standby section and asked whether we can shorten the activation lead time for our primary region to 15 minutes for critical routes (payments, auth) while leaving a 45-minute window for analytics/low-priority jobs.

Key asks from FinLedger:
- RTO target for critical routes: 15 minutes (from current 30m)
- RPO tolerance unchanged at 5 minutes for critical routes
- Clear priority window where we can preempt warm-standby capacity for these routes during incident activation

I attached the ops questions spreadsheet with a few implementation clarifications. Can Redwood confirm whether this is feasible without impacting the existing warm-standby pricing/commitment? If there are cost or SLA trade-offs we should know, please flag them.

Appreciate a quick read — our contract deadline is the 12th.

Best,
Alice
Alice Hart
Director, Infrastructure & Ops
FinLedger
[Attachment: finledger-ops-questions.xlsx]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Warm-Standby activation lead time — proposed amendment

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. Short answer: we can support a prioritized 15-minute activation path for critical routes, but it requires a scoped amendment to the Warm-Standby activation policy and an operational commitment on pre-warming and priority routing.

High-level implications:
- We will reserve a small pre-warmed pool in the primary region specifically tagged for "critical" routes. That pool must be maintained during your declared business hours (we can align on PST business window).
- There is a small incremental monthly charge for dedicated pre-warm capacity and peak-surge liability if activation occurs outside agreed windows.
- We can keep RPO at 5 minutes for critical and unchanged for other traffic.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kim (cc'd) to outline the operational changes and any monitoring hooks we need to add to the runbook.
2) Karthik to prepare the contract addendum language and updated pricing table.
3) I'll send an updated proposal PDF that shows the carveout and priority window wording.

I'll attach a draft proposal (v2) by EOD. Is a Friday (3/9) signature reasonable for you?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-warm-standby-proposal-v2.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Warm-Standby activation lead time — operational notes

Alice —

Quick operational notes on the pre-warm approach:
- Priority routing: we'll tag the payment/auth routes at the edge and attach a priority flag. The runtime will prefer the pre-warmed pool for these flags.
- Observability: we'll add a per-route activation timer metric and an alert for pre-warm exhaustion.
- Failure modes: if pre-warm pool is exhausted, requests fall back to standard pool and activation will follow the standard 30m path. We'll include an automatic fallback notice in the response headers for audit.

Questions for your ops team (from the spreadsheet):
- Can you confirm expected concurrent critical RPS during peak? (helps size pool)
- Do you need pre-warm coverage 24/7 or only during business hours?

Assuming we get concurrent RPS estimates, we can size the pool and give a firm incremental cost estimate.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Warm-Standby activation lead time — commercial addendum

Alice / team —

Based on Marissa and Kim's notes, I've drafted the contractual addendum language and a pricing delta for the dedicated pre-warm pool. Key points:
- Amendment: "Customer may opt for a Critical-Route Pre-warm (CRP) for selected route IDs. Redwood will maintain a dedicated pre-warmed capacity sized to the customer's concurrent RPS estimate. Activation SLA for CRP routes: RTO 15 minutes; RPO 5 minutes."
- Pricing: Monthly reserved pre-warm fee + per-activation surge fee if activation triggers outside agreed windows or if pool capacity is exceeded.
- Term: minimum 3-month commitment for CRP sizing predictability.

I've attached the draft language to the HubSpot deal and left line-item pricing options for the pool sizes we discussed (small/med/large). Naomi — can you confirm billing setup and whether we can offer a one-time onboarding credit?

Alice — if that looks reasonable I'll convert the addendum to DocuSign and share for signature. We can also include an operational runbook appendix so your SREs have the routing flags and metrics.

Thanks,
Karthik
